# Model Router

> Model Router (`model-router`) is an open-source Claude Code plugin that keeps the Claude model and reasoning effort Claude names for every agent Claude Code starts (subagents, agent-team teammates and workflow stages) inside the user's limits, fills in the effort when only a model is named, and runs a call Claude marks as a redo with more effort or on a stronger model. It picks among Claude models only (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus, Fable). It isn't a proxy to non-Claude models. An independent project by Cris Nahine (https://github.com/crisnahine), not made or endorsed by Anthropic. Apache-2.0 license. Needs Claude Code 2.1.329 or later and Python 3.9 or later. Site: https://crisnahine.github.io/claude-code-model-router/

Facts, each with its source:

- The ladder: lookup runs on Haiku at medium effort, standard on Sonnet at medium, complex on Opus at high, hardest on Opus at xhigh, frontier on Fable at high. A model named on a call stands for its lowest level and runs at that level's effort when nobody named one; Opus named with xhigh or max is hardest. A call that names no model runs where the order below puts it, and on its parent's model only when nothing there names one. The router never reads a brief. Source: plugins/model-router/config/models.json and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
- Redo escalation: only a call whose description starts with "Redo:" is a redo, which Claude marks when a check failed or a result fell short. One that names a model or effort asking for more than the run it redoes runs as named; one that names the same or less climbs anyway. Otherwise it climbs from the run of the same agent and description that finished in the same session in the last 30 minutes, or, when there is none, from what the call would run at unmarked: one effort step up on that run's model while it was below high, else on the next stronger model, else one more effort step. A run inside a subagent at its parent's effort, which the router can't see, skips the same-model step. When CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL or CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT sets the effort, a redo goes straight to the next stronger model; under CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE only the effort climbs. Workflow stages are never redone. No description text is stored: a redo finds its run by a hash. /model-router:usage counts redos by level. Source: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/GUIDE.md.
- Who decides the model, strongest first: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE, CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_SUBAGENT_MODEL for a workflow agent whose call names no model, a model named on the call, a per-agent rule in model-router.json, the agent's own model field, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, then the parent's model. A model from the call, a rule, the agent's own field or the parent is held to the max_tier cap and raised to a rule's level, and a teammate whose parent is weaker than Sonnet starts on Sonnet. A model one of the three environment variables sets is neither capped nor raised, and on the fallback path a call made inside a subagent isn't capped, since its parent's model can't be seen. A call left on CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL or the parent's model gets no effort from the router. A fork always runs on its conversation's model, and the router leaves it alone. Source: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
- Benchmarks: today's plugin, where Claude names each call's model and effort, has not been benchmarked yet. Every stored row measured an older design, in which the router read the brief and picked the level itself. On the six harder tasks of the latest pilot, that older router cost more per run than Claude Code with no plugin (raw rows in bench/results/pilot/). The full benchmark measured that older routing code at commit <!-- bench:opus.commit -->780ee86<!-- /bench -->, on easier tasks. On an Opus 5.5 session the router solved <!-- bench:opus.solved.router -->70 of 70<!-- /bench --> runs, as many as Claude Code's defaults, for <!-- bench:opus.pooled.router -->$0.121<!-- /bench --> per solved task against the defaults' <!-- bench:opus.pooled.defaults -->$0.151<!-- /bench -->. It isn't the cheapest setup on these tasks: every subagent on Haiku at high effort also solved <!-- bench:opus.solved.haiku-high -->70 of 70<!-- /bench -->, for <!-- bench:opus.pooled.haiku-high -->$0.075<!-- /bench -->. By task class, none of these runs supports a verdict under the benchmark's current rules: they ran before subagent commands ran in a sandbox, and the router ran in other batches than its baselines. Source: docs/BENCHMARKS.md and docs/TRACEABILITY.md row S4.15.
- Privacy: no prompt, brief, path or code leaves the machine, and the plugin makes no network call. Source: docs/SECURITY.md.
- Upgrading from 0.1.2: the options priority, agent_pins, main_effort, update_check and strong_agent_gate are gone, and a value saved for one of them is ignored. A saved routing_mode of advise reads as off, so set auto in /config to route. The /model-router:ship and /model-router:refresh skills and the model-router:deep-solver and model-router:docs-researcher agents are gone. learned.json, prompts.json, upstream.json and mod.json in the plugin's data folder are no longer read and can be deleted, and a main or crew key in model-router.json is ignored. Source: CHANGELOG.md.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crisnahine/claude-code-model-router/main/README.md): what it does, install, options, compatibility
- [Questions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crisnahine/claude-code-model-router/main/docs/FAQ.md): short answers to common questions
- [Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crisnahine/claude-code-model-router/main/docs/GUIDE.md): commands, every option, who decides the model, workflows and ultracode, limits, providers, update and uninstall
- [Built on the docs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crisnahine/claude-code-model-router/main/docs/CLAUDE_CODE_DOCS.md): each Claude Code and Claude docs rule the plugin follows, with its doc page and test
- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crisnahine/claude-code-model-router/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the two paths, the ladder, the decision and its order of authority
- [Glossary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crisnahine/claude-code-model-router/main/GLOSSARY.md): the project's own words
- [Benchmarks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crisnahine/claude-code-model-router/main/docs/BENCHMARKS.md): cost per solved task of an older design against Claude Code without the plugin, with raw data
- [Security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crisnahine/claude-code-model-router/main/docs/SECURITY.md): what reaches the network and who can influence routing
- [Performance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crisnahine/claude-code-model-router/main/docs/PERFORMANCE.md): hook latency, state size and the context the plugin adds
